acts.title: SHELTER UNDER ARMS
acts.for: Protect a fleeing keeper from armed pursuit at the teaching-house doorway. Settle immediate custody and discover the threatened Crown post through people and physical evidence. Hrill has direct fighting and judgment work.
acts.takes: Custody, bodily safety, equipment and freedom can be lost through actual opposed action. Doorway cover and side escape work. No mandatory injury, enlistment, pursuit or choice to sail. Early surrender and refusal are possible.

acts.title: REACH THE LIGHT
acts.for: Reach Greywatch by actual voyage if chosen, reconnoitre, enter via quay or cistern, help honest defenders, remove transport/blockade or assault resources. Discover this independent company's aim to establish an imperial foothold.
acts.takes: Exposed landings, hostile bows, stone stairs, finite supplies and real enemy tactics create risk. No compulsory swimming or automatic equipment change. Gained allies and defeated assets change the next situation permanently.

acts.title: WHO HOLDS THE SHORE
acts.for: Defend, relieve, extract, force surrender or otherwise settle the surviving seizure attempt. Deny a real restorationist base; no need to pursue Hanzo or accept an endless campaign. Earlier success can conclude the story.
acts.takes: Post, stores, freedom and lives face actual executable operations. Defeat and retreat remain possible; no prescribed death, betrayal or revenge raid. Cancel dependent operations when people or means are gone.

due_beats.title: Maro Quist reads it to the end
due_beats.summary: The magistrate reads everything put in front of him, at his own pace, while you wait -- and then explains accurately why it is not his to act on
due_beats.onscreen_if: On an actual petition presented to Maro Quist; date is opportunity backstop, not an invented offscreen petitioner.
due_beats.narrative:
**The wall, in the person of a decent man.**

Seventy-one, upright, chain always worn. He does not interrupt and cannot be
interrupted. He reads the whole thing -- actually reads it, in front of you, at
his own pace, while you stand there -- and then repeats your position back to
you more accurately than you put it.

And then tells you exactly why it is not his.

The watch is under a written standing order. He is not corrupt, he is not
frightened, and he is not persuadable, because he is **right**. A baron's son
with a knife is weather, and you do not sue the weather.

If he reads it twice, he has changed his mind, and the room should know it.

due_beats.title: Ivo Calder folds
due_beats.summary: The assayer who signed what he should not have has kept his original notes, moved them twice, and collapses completely the moment an independent reading appears
due_beats.narrative:
Fifty, distinguished, guild indigo, instruments kept beautifully, and he has
not slept properly in six weeks.

He has the whole defence prepared and wants to deliver it; a question he has not
anticipated stops him dead. What he wants is to be told that what he signed was
reasonable.

**There is no middle with him.** Vigorous defence, and then everything, in one
breath, the moment an independent reading appears. He has not destroyed the
original notes and has moved them twice.

What this buys is **a name** -- who is actually paying the Baron -- not a
conviction. The man who is paying is not in this city and does not die on the
sand.

# The Crown's Last Light — selected preparation

27 October 2026. “Continue” follows the recommended beacon premise. The GM
stated that interpretation before preparation. Reuse the explicit interview:
dangerous knightly action, rescue, tactics, exploration and honor; a reluctant
fighter, no compulsory killing, animal hunt, distant summons or new enlistment.
Compress logistics. Trouble reaches his present shore. Preparation holds
d25/dusk minute92; opening resumes here without assuming Edda's answer, travel,
rest, equipment change or acceptance of a commission.

## Experience and global conflict

Avel Veyr wants Greywatch's signal, defensible landing and thirty days' military
stores as a recruitment base for renewed draconic imperial rule. She believes
small independent communities will eventually accept a ruler who can enforce
order. She has committed her remaining savings and six-person company to taking
it. Corporal Dera Venn refuses to surrender royal ground or its civilians.
Avel will use lethal force against armed resistance; prisoners are leverage and
labor, not automatic murder victims. Pike wants his outstanding fee, not empire.
His pursuit of the keeper threatens the village's hospitality and her freedom.
Hrill is the trained close fighter immediately beside the threatened person.
Protecting her can lead to protecting a real Crown garrison; no oath is required.

This advances the global restoration conflict causally: a landing, stores and
signal become contested capacity. Saving the post denies that foothold. Avel is
independent of Hanzo. No secret orders, possession, endless reinforcements,
reactivated tournament scheme or cancellation of Halla's victory. Hanzo's actual
withdrawal and parked household remain unchanged. The wider question is whether
fear and promised order can rebuild the old dominion, opposed by people who
choose mutual defense. A local victory can finish this adventure completely.

## Starting situation, geography and timing

Greywatch is new minor local geography on the outer eastern lake shore, two
hours by ordinary small boat south of Listening Reeds' outer landing, bypassing
the longer inner route through Narrow Water. It is not an ancient marked fort
from Selith's chart. Flint Cove is fifteen minutes rowing south of its quay.
No change to existing Bell Reed/White Shingle/Narrow Water travel distances.
The post is Crown land; Listening Reeds remains independent, not under its law.

Initial present setting: Avel's six-person party has reached Greywatch's outer
yard by its inland track and demands surrender. Dera and two guards hold the
tower with civilian Bess. No assault, injury or capture has yet been resolved.
Keeper Halwen, outside the gate when the company arrived, took the post's skiff
to the nearby independent settlement for help. Pike's contracted boat followed
her visible course. Establish these starting placements as the selected premise,
not as outcomes of a played rescue or a failed offscreen resistance roll.

Opening contact at minute94: Halwen runs from her tied skiff into the teaching
house doorway. Mar and Toll are ten yards behind her with drawn weapons; Pike
and Arlo remain in their moored boat thirty yards beyond the doorway, with Arlo's
bow available but not aimed or drawn. No arrow, attack or PC reaction assumed.
Edda stands at the doorway from the preceding scene, Hrill beside the table,
Selith at the table. Grey Heron is on the same village landing, forty yards
from the house. Hrill has a sheathed sword and an available shortbow, lowered
and unnocked, twenty arrows; mail and shield stowed aboard.
Do not silently equip anything. Halwen asks shelter; Mar demands she come out.
The threshold is a physical choke, the records room a retreat, the side door
opens onto a reed-bank footpath. House walls stop sight and ordinary arrows.

Unopposed intentions, never predetermined outcomes: Pike first demands custody,
then orders Mar/Toll to seize Halwen if they can do so without a general village
battle. If met by an armed defender he demands passage, attempts a brief rush
only if numerical advantage remains, and withdraws at serious injury or if
villagers mobilize. He will not burn the village or shoot children. Returning
news to Avel takes two actual hours. Avel cannot know the encounter meanwhile.
At d26/dawn Avel may attempt her tower breach if she still has at least three
fit fighters and the ladder. Evaluate resistance and prior changes first.

## Cast, organization and finite resources

All sheets, personality scores, inventory and placements are in TypeDB and the
companion setup manifest. Human NPCs have no Luck or spells. No horses.

for five),60crossbow bolts,12bundles beacon wood and2oil jars for lighting,

Actionable truth has physical sources. Pike's waterproof fee chit in boat locker
names Avel,12GP remainder and Greywatch landing. Pike can admit it; captured crew
know employer/location but not exact fee. Avel's kit holds a stitched dragon
banner, recruitment promises and a sketch marking the quay/stores/signal.
Her spoken demands and soldiers' testimony also reveal political purpose.
Halwen's maintenance tools carry a narrow iron cistern key; Dera/Bess can give
the same approach, and the exposed stone drainage arch can be found physically.
No failed Perception roll deletes it: a failed search takes fifteen minutes and
risks a sentry's observation, then another approach remains. No universal key.
Initial GM truths attach only to actual participants' knowledge. Hrill learns
only doorstep observations at opening. No advance knowledge of Avel, purpose,
enemy totals, contract, cistern or impending dawn attempt. Edda/Selith know no
more than their direct observations. No information reaches Avel until a real
messenger returns. Hanzo hears nothing automatically.

## Three acts, subject to player changes

I — Shelter under arms. Protect Halwen or otherwise settle the attempted seizure.
Immediate win: safe civilian and a reduced, driven-off, captured or negotiated
pursuit party. Investigate physical boat/keeper evidence to learn the post is
threatened. If Hrill refuses, Selith can shelter Halwen and residents resist;
resolve actual contest, no mandatory death or destruction. Enemy withdrawal
changes later blockade resources. End when help/withdrawal is decided.

II — Reach and change the siege. Actual2h passage required if chosen, with
equipment/rest decisions respected. Enemy cove/boat can be disabled, bought out
or captured; infiltrate water stair, relieve garrison, recover supplies, scout
enemy positions. Discovery of imperial purpose changes an apparent local seizure
into an attempt to build real restorationist capacity. No second required fight.
If Pike is neutralized there is no blockade; if Avel already surrenders skip
later conflict. Warnings are visible sentries, ladder and shouted demands.

III — End the surviving operation. Defend against an executable breach, organize
a sortie, surround the company, secure surrender, or evacuate while denying
stores. Loss of landing/resources matters even if Avel escapes. Possible durable
endings: post retained; post abandoned with all people saved; enemy occupation;
partial rescue; lawful custody. Avel can actually win but no ending is compulsory.

### G1 — Doorway seizure
Purpose: immediate protection/close action, establishes opposing custody claim.
Actor: Pike wants keeper isolated, sends Mar/Toll only; prerequisites: four fit
crew and boat reaching the village by the followed visible route. Scene geometry
above; house and side path are real cover and escape. Earliest opening94; no
deadline expressed as automatic injury. Mar's first demand gives warning; rush
only after PC response and if a feasible advantage remains. Sword55 vs Hrill's
chosen defense, Toll club45; NPC2AP each, no surprise/free attack. PC may bar
door, fight, warn, question, seize boat or withdraw. Start encounter and initiative
if violence becomes immediate; ask PC defense and special effects. Brawn contested
for a forced door; braced inner table makes it harder; no silent roll before
player chooses. Negotiation Influence vs Pike Willpower45, supported by actual
armed resistance and self-interest; intimidation can change circumstances.

rules, never automatic victim abduction. Retreat into room/side path remains.

### G2 — Rock quay and cistern approach

quay30ft across, stone chest-high bollards, stairs climb40ft to yard; two abreast,

yard40x50ft, tower door barred from within. Cistern arch60ft north of quay,
exposed maintenance ledge3ftwide above water, locked hatch, dry stairs into
ground room. No obligatory swimming. Avel places Enna at quay overlook, Corl
on track, remaining three with her in yard only after actual opening changes.

needs no discovery roll. Engineering can identify safe access, Athletics for a
rushed exposed climb only, not a routine stair toll. Defender may shoot exposed
hostiles only with clear line and in combat order; cover and withdrawal work.
Fall requires actual failure at rail gap with failed save per rules; ordinary
walking isn't a trap. Failed stealth brings challenge or contact, not teleporting
all enemies to entry. Reaching tower lets Hrill organize practical defense.

### G3 — Flint Cove contract and boat
Purpose: remove paid transport dependency. Beach60ft, grounded bow, chest and
supplies under oilcloth10ft back; foot track to tower is20minutes. Whichever
Pike crew actually remain are here after their two-hour return, not also at
village or blockade. Written contract is discoverable by opening unlocked locker;
search costs time if contested, no roll for reading obvious words. Pike protects
boat but bargains at credible defeat; no required12GP payment by PC. Open-water
escape possible; opposition Boating60 against actual pursuer skill when chased.
Cut moorings can inconvenience, not sink sound hull; damaging it uses actual
AP/HP and weapons. Yielded contract/testimony supports lawful action. Removing
crew/boat/pay bargain cancels blockade, no replacement vessel.

### G4 — Breach or sortie
Purpose: decisive physical action over living people and post. Prerequisites:
Avel free,3fit fighters, ladder, actual intact route; at26dawn earliest after
reports/recovery. If conditions fail cancel attempt. Preparation takes20minutes
with visible ladder movement; tower defenders can act before breach. Ladder
leans against20ftwall, room for one climber at a time; shutters give defenders
cover, not immunity. Opposed Engineering40 vs Dera Engineering45 for useful
breach placement/defense preparation, then actual attacks/climbs/door damage,
not one opposed roll that kills a garrison. Door AP4 HP20. NPC crossbow reload
and arrow consumption persist. Fire pots only if Avel still has them and staff
can escape through ground floor; ignition/fire harm use fetched rules, never
automatic tower conflagration. Hrill can hold narrow ground, topple ladder,
sortie or call terms; all can be consequential. Failed defense can lose post,
capture or wound through actual rolls. Surrender/withdrawal terminate dependent
operations. No compulsory duel. Civilians can evacuate by cistern or skiff if
available; respecting survival can trump possession for Dera.

finite named cast and CFI sheets; mapped approaches; political evidence and
per-character ignorance; conditional operations and permanent asset losses.
Refusal leaves independent actors and real opposed resolution. Authorities can
help after travel. Pike negotiations materially remove blockade. Existing allies
are competent and retain consent. Early Avel defeat ends her operation. Cistern
first and cove first both work. No prescribed harm or deity/possession mechanism.

no clock advance during design. New future successes remain not-yet-true.

due_beats.title: Maro Quist reads it to the end
due_beats.summary: The magistrate reads everything put in front of him, at his own pace, while you wait -- and then explains accurately why it is not his to act on
due_beats.onscreen_if: On an actual petition presented to Maro Quist; date is opportunity backstop, not an invented offscreen petitioner.
due_beats.narrative:
**The wall, in the person of a decent man.**

Seventy-one, upright, chain always worn. He does not interrupt and cannot be
interrupted. He reads the whole thing -- actually reads it, in front of you, at
his own pace, while you stand there -- and then repeats your position back to
you more accurately than you put it.

And then tells you exactly why it is not his.

The watch is under a written standing order. He is not corrupt, he is not
frightened, and he is not persuadable, because he is **right**. A baron's son
with a knife is weather, and you do not sue the weather.

If he reads it twice, he has changed his mind, and the room should know it.

due_beats.title: Ivo Calder folds
due_beats.summary: The assayer who signed what he should not have has kept his original notes, moved them twice, and collapses completely the moment an independent reading appears
due_beats.narrative:
Fifty, distinguished, guild indigo, instruments kept beautifully, and he has
not slept properly in six weeks.

He has the whole defence prepared and wants to deliver it; a question he has not
anticipated stops him dead. What he wants is to be told that what he signed was
reasonable.

**There is no middle with him.** Vigorous defence, and then everything, in one
breath, the moment an independent reading appears. He has not destroyed the
original notes and has moved them twice.

What this buys is **a name** -- who is actually paying the Baron -- not a
conviction. The man who is paying is not in this city and does not die on the
sand.

due_beats.title: Maro Quist reads it to the end
due_beats.summary: The magistrate reads everything put in front of him, at his own pace, while you wait -- and then explains accurately why it is not his to act on
due_beats.onscreen_if: On an actual petition presented to Maro Quist; date is opportunity backstop, not an invented offscreen petitioner.
due_beats.narrative:
**The wall, in the person of a decent man.**

Seventy-one, upright, chain always worn. He does not interrupt and cannot be
interrupted. He reads the whole thing -- actually reads it, in front of you, at
his own pace, while you stand there -- and then repeats your position back to
you more accurately than you put it.

And then tells you exactly why it is not his.

The watch is under a written standing order. He is not corrupt, he is not
frightened, and he is not persuadable, because he is **right**. A baron's son
with a knife is weather, and you do not sue the weather.

If he reads it twice, he has changed his mind, and the room should know it.

due_beats.title: Ivo Calder folds
due_beats.summary: The assayer who signed what he should not have has kept his original notes, moved them twice, and collapses completely the moment an independent reading appears
due_beats.narrative:
Fifty, distinguished, guild indigo, instruments kept beautifully, and he has
not slept properly in six weeks.

He has the whole defence prepared and wants to deliver it; a question he has not
anticipated stops him dead. What he wants is to be told that what he signed was
reasonable.

**There is no middle with him.** Vigorous defence, and then everything, in one
breath, the moment an independent reading appears. He has not destroyed the
original notes and has moved them twice.

What this buys is **a name** -- who is actually paying the Baron -- not a
conviction. The man who is paying is not in this city and does not die on the
sand.
